info.name: Kongila — complete API
info.description:
Every endpoint in the three Kongila apps, with a successful call, the
unauthenticated case, the wrong-role case and the wrong-owner case where one
applies.

HOW TO USE
1. Import this file and `kongila.postman_environment.json`.
2. Fill in the environment: supabaseUrl, supabaseAnonKey, the base URLs, and
   four sets of credentials (client, talent, admin, a second client).
3. Run folder 00 first. It signs each account in and saves the tokens.
4. Run the folders in order. Later ones reuse ids captured by earlier ones.
5. Run folder 26 last, or first if you only want to check RLS.

WHAT TO WATCH
- Folders 25 and 26 are the ones that matter for release. Everything in them
  must fail. A 200 there is a finding.
- Requests named NEGATIVE are expected to fail. Their tests assert the
  failure, so a green tick means the refusal worked.
- Remotan is dormant and excluded, apart from one check that its /api/db no
  longer accepts an unauthenticated write.

NOT COVERED, AND WHY
- Raw file bytes. Postman cannot carry a file inside a saved collection, so
  the upload folder gets a signed URL and stops. Do the PUT by hand once.
- /api/clients and /api/talents are covered in the resource endpoint folder.
  The portals no longer use /api/db; folder 23 tests its read-only
  compatibility behavior.

item.name: 00 Authentication and tokens
item.description:
Get a token before anything else.

Postman cannot sign in to Supabase for you with the anon key alone, so the
three sign-in requests below call Supabase Auth directly and save the access
token into the environment. Fill in supabaseUrl, supabaseAnonKey and the three
sets of credentials first.

Every other folder reads one of clientToken, talentToken or adminToken.

item.name: 05 Matching and shortlists
item.description:
Operations submits candidates; the client decides on them.

Submitted candidates are written as `proposed`. Shortlisted is the client's
verdict, and matches_status_check allows only proposed, shortlisted, rejected
and accepted.

request.description: When this is the last candidate on the request, operations is notified.
Should be 409. A rejection with no reason is a dead end for operations.

item.name: 06 Vetting and assessments
item.description:
Scores and the stage pipeline are operations-only. The candidate drives
stages 4 to 6 through /api/vetting/advance, and submits assessment answers
(not scores) through /api/assessments/submit.

request.description: The grade is computed server-side from the scores. Only this candidate's row is written.

item.name: NEGATIVE candidate records their own scores

request.description: Applied cannot jump to Deployed. Should be 409.
Answers only. The score is computed server-side from the answer key, which never leaves the server.

item.name: NEGATIVE submit a score instead of answers

request.description: The score field is ignored. Check the response: autoScore must reflect the answers, not 100.

item.name: NEGATIVE submit the same assessment twice

request.description: Should be 409. Without this a candidate could retake until they passed.

08 Interviews
item.description:
Scheduling, confirming, rescheduling, cancelling and rating.

Times are stored as a UTC instant plus the zone each side entered. The
service checks for clashes and refuses a slot in the past.

item.description:
An offer is raised, approved and sent by Kongila, then accepted or declined
by the candidate. The contract is created only on acceptance.

item.name: 10 Contracts
item.description:
Statuses are the nine contracts_status_check permits. The admin panel's
words (Draft, Signed, Active, Voided) are mapped server-side; Draft means
pending and Voided means terminated.

item.name: ADMIN draft a contract by hand

request.description: Starts at `pending`. The panel used to build this in the browser with status 'Draft', which the column refuses.

item.name: ADMIN send a contract out for signature

request.description: This used to alert 'Reminder sent' and send nothing.
Sets fully_signed and moves the request to Onboarding. Blocked if the candidate has outstanding compliance documents.
Maps to `terminated` and reopens the request behind it.
A pending contract cannot jump to active. Should be 409.

item.name: NEGATIVE client changes a contract status

request.description: The older whole-snapshot route. Prefer POST /api/contracts/status with action=create.

item.name: NEGATIVE two published templates for one line

request.description: Should be 409. Two published templates for the same line means whichever is read first decides what a contract says.

item.name: 12 Signatures and compliance
item.description:
The document text is built server-side and hashed, so what was shown and
what was signed cannot drift. IP and user agent come from the request.

request.description: Decided server-side. The dashboard used to work this out by matching file names.

item.name: NEGATIVE mandatory document with an owner

request.description: A mandatory document applies to everyone, so it has no owner. Should be 422.
user_id and status are not editable here. The old route spread the body straight onto the row.
Hides rather than deletes. This path was unreachable before: the route had two PUT blocks and this was the second.

item.name: 13 Documents and uploads
item.description:
Uploading is two steps: ask /api/uploads for a signed URL, then PUT the
bytes to it. The server chooses the object path from the session, so a path
cannot be aimed at someone else's folder.

The second request below is the raw upload. Set the body to `binary` and pick
a file; Postman cannot send a file from a saved collection.

item.name: NEGATIVE talent asks for a compliance upload

request.description: Should be 403. Only operations upload compliance templates.
Call this after the bytes are uploaded, with the storedUrl from the upload ticket.

  "issuingBody": "Amazon Web Services",

18 Finance (client and talent)
item.description:
A client sees their own invoices. A candidate sees their own payouts and
no invoices at all, because an invoice is between Kongila and the client and
shows the margin.

request.description: Must not return invoices. Either 403, or an empty list with no margin in it.
Unauthenticated by design.
Should be 410. Kept as a loud refusal rather than deleted, because it used to create a contract the moment a client clicked Hire.

item.name: 19 Finance (operations)
item.description:
Fees, invoice generation, sending, settlement and payouts.

Set the four service-line margins in `fee_config` before anything else here
will produce sensible numbers.

request.description: Dry run. Shows what would be generated and what would be skipped, and why.
Issues the number, sets the due date from the contract's payment terms and emails the PDF.
Releases the candidate's payout. Super admin or finance only.
Should be 409. A paid invoice is reversed with a credit note.

item.name: 20 Payroll
item.description:
Monthly, prorated by calendar days, for Managed Workforce and Outsourcing
only. A Placement candidate is employed by the client directly and a Project
is paid on delivery, so including either would pay somebody twice.

request.description: Shows the entries and the skipped contracts with the reason for each.
The file an operator hands to whoever moves the money.

item.name: 25 Cross-user isolation
item.description:
The folder to run before signing anything off.

Every request here uses one person's token against another person's record
and must fail. Run them after the other folders have populated the
environment with real ids, and set otherTalentId, otherDocumentId and
otherTicketId by hand from a second account's data.

request.description: Either 403, or an empty list. It must not return the other candidate's documents.
Paste an expired or revoked token into expiredToken. Should be 401.
Set malformedToken to any nonsense string. Should be 401.

If any returns rows, RLS is not on for that table and nothing else in this
collection matters.
